Okay, let's tackle this query step by step. The user provided a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with specific hypotheses and wants me to determine if each hypothesis is Entailment, Contradiction, or NotMentioned based on the document. The key here is to carefully review each hypothesis against the exact text of the NDA, using the provided span indices as evidence.

Starting with hypothesis nda-11: "Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information." The NDA doesn't mention reverse engineering anywhere. The closest related section is Paragraph 4, which talks about using information only for specified purposes, but there's no mention of reverse engineering. So, this is NotMentioned.

Next, nda-16: "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." Looking at span 33, it says that at the end of the agreement, proprietary data must be returned or destroyed. This directly supports the hypothesis, so it's Entailment.

For nda-15: "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." Paragraphs 28 and 29 explicitly state that no rights are granted, so this is Entailment.

nda-10: "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated." There's no mention of the agreement's existence being confidential, so NotMentioned.

nda-2: "Confidential Information shall only include technical information." The definition in span 8 includes non-technical items like business plans and financial info, so this contradicts the hypothesis. Therefore, Contradiction.

nda-1: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." The NDA doesn't specify that all info must be explicitly identified, so NotMentioned.

nda-19: "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement." Span 31 and 32 mention obligations remaining for three years after termination, so Entailment.

nda-12: "Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information." Span 24 allows independent development, so Entailment.

nda-20: "Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information." Span 27 allows one copy to be retained by legal counsel, so Entailment.

nda-3: "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." Span 15 mentions oral disclosures, so Entailment.

nda-18: "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives." No mention of solicitation, so NotMentioned.

nda-7: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties..." Span 26 allows sharing with employees and consultants under certain conditions, so Entailment.

nda-17: "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances." The NDA doesn't mention copying, so NotMentioned.

nda-8: "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose..." Span 26 mentions notifying the disclosing party before disclosure to a regulatory body, so Entailment.

nda-13: "Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party." Span 23 allows receiving info from third parties if they don't have a secrecy obligation, so Entailment.

nda-5: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees." Span 26 allows sharing with employees who have confidentiality agreements, so Entailment.

nda-4: "Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Span 13 and 26 restrict use to specified purposes, so Entailment.
